concepts.name: Group
concepts.definition: A set with an associative binary operation, an identity element, and inverses.

concepts.name: Subgroup
concepts.definition: A subset of a group that is itself a group under the same operation.

dependsOn.name: Group
dependsOn.reason: A subgroup is a subset of a group closed under its operation.

concepts.name: Normal subgroup
concepts.definition: A subgroup $N$ of $G$ with $gNg^{-1} = N$ for every $g \in G$.

dependsOn.name: Subgroup
dependsOn.reason: A normal subgroup is a subgroup invariant under conjugation.

concepts.name: Homomorphism
concepts.definition: A map $\varphi: G \to H$ between groups with $\varphi(ab) = \varphi(a)\varphi(b)$.

dependsOn.name: Group
dependsOn.reason: A homomorphism maps one group to another, preserving the operation.

concepts.name: Kernel
concepts.definition: The set of elements a homomorphism sends to the identity: $\ker\varphi = \{ g \in G : \varphi(g) = e \}$.

dependsOn.name: Homomorphism
dependsOn.reason: The kernel is defined for a homomorphism.

concepts.name: Quotient group
concepts.definition: The group $G/N$ of cosets of a normal subgroup $N$, with $(aN)(bN) = abN$.

dependsOn.name: Group
dependsOn.reason: G/N is built from a group G.

dependsOn.name: Normal subgroup
dependsOn.reason: Cosets only multiply consistently when N is normal.

concepts.name: First Isomorphism Theorem
concepts.definition: For a homomorphism $\varphi: G \to H$, $G/\ker\varphi$ is isomorphic to $\operatorname{im}\varphi$.

dependsOn.name: Homomorphism
dependsOn.reason: The theorem starts from a homomorphism φ: G → H.

dependsOn.name: Kernel
dependsOn.reason: It divides G by the kernel of φ.

dependsOn.name: Quotient group
dependsOn.reason: G / ker φ is a quotient group.

aToB.explanation: The kernel of any homomorphism is a normal subgroup of its domain.

bToA.explanation: Every normal subgroup N is the kernel of the projection $G \to G/N$.

aToB.explanation: $G/N$ comes with the canonical projection $g \mapsto gN$, a surjective homomorphism.

bToA.explanation: Up to isomorphism, the image of a homomorphism is a quotient of its domain.
